annotations.title: Create and approve a content brief

description: Create a reviewed brief with required brand_id, source_topic_id when starting from a saved topic, and pillar_id when available. The API approves this supplied brief, making it ready for item generation. Optional facts (at most 20, at most 5 must_use) are user-supplied claims the article cites; they need the v2 article pipeline (409 article_pipeline_not_v2 otherwise) and a refused fact is a 422 with nothing saved. Optional article_spec marks elements (citations, stats, key_takeaways, quotes, faq, comparison_table, toc, relevant_links, products) required, optional or off and sets citation, FAQ, length and voice targets; omit it for the standard article. A required source must also be in source_urls. Optional article_template names a built-in key (standard, listicle, how_to, comparison) or an owned template UUID: the brief copies that template's article spec, target words and heading roles when it is saved, and keeps that copy even if the template is edited later. A field you also send is kept as sent. An unknown or foreign template is a 422.

items.description:
A fact you supply for the article to cite (request).

One line of plain text, at most 200 characters, with no Markdown, HTML,
links or ``[[``/``]]``. ``source_url`` is optional: its page is fetched
at generation and the fact is cited to it only when the page states every
figure and name in the fact; otherwise the fact is used without a link
(a regulated workspace leaves it out). A ``source_url`` the brand source
policy or the workspace's blocked hosts refuse is a 422
(``user_fact_source_url_ineligible``), and workspaces with
regulated-content settings must supply one (422
``user_fact_source_url_required``). Generation applies these rules again
and leaves out a fact that no longer meets them. At most 20 facts, at
most 5 with ``priority=must_use``.

article_spec.description:
What the article must contain, may contain, or must leave out.

Every key is optional and an absent key takes its default, so ``{}`` asks
for nothing beyond the standard article. ``elements`` names only the
elements you change; the rest keep their defaults (citations, stats, key
takeaways, quotes, FAQ, relevant links and products optional; comparison
table, steps and table of contents off). Citations cannot be off; steps
and comparison tables accept required, optional and off.

``elements`` wins over a detail section: an element set to ``off`` ignores
its details (``faq.questions``, ``products``, ``relevant_links``, ``stats``),
which are kept so switching the element back on restores them. For
products and relevant links, the element mode is only the default for new
items; each item's own ``requirement`` is what applies while the element is
on. ``reading_level.requirement: off`` means the level is not judged, the
same as leaving ``level`` empty.

status.description:
Status of a background job.

Terminal states: ``completed``, ``completed_with_errors``, ``failed``,
``cancelled``. Active (in-progress) states: ``queued``, ``running``.

``awaiting_review`` is a third class: not terminal (work may resume after a
human action) and not active (no automatic progress is being made). Pollers
should treat it as stop-and-review rather than keep waiting for a terminal
status. It is intentionally in neither ``is_terminal`` nor ``is_active``.
status.title: JobStatus
